body: Team name: Prisma
Team leader name: Jan Daniel Gonzalvo
Problem Statement: Data Studio dashboards take hours of clicks and design skill
slides.notes: We are team Prisma. The problem: people who know their data (analysts, managers, students) can't easily turn their questions into a good Data Studio dashboard, because building one takes hours of clicking plus design skill.

Democratizing Google Data Studio is an agentic web app. You bring data (a CSV, GCS or BigQuery tables) and a goal. An agent interviews you about audience, questions and KPIs, designs the dashboard as an HTML prototype you can comment on, then compiles a recipe and builds the real Data Studio dashboard in a visible Chrome window. The goal is a working dashboard link, not a mockup; the full compiler and live build are still being finished.

body: Different: other tools generate charts or SQL; we build a real, editable Data Studio report from a compiled recipe.
How it solves the problem: a short interview turns business questions into a Dashboard Spec; click-to-comment fixes the design before any build.
USP: an agent harness with three memories built to learn from every build (retrieval, consolidation: planned), plus a deterministic engine that clicks Data Studio for you.
Opportunity: every team on Google Workspace already has Data Studio and BigQuery.
slides.notes: Three answers to the template's questions. Different: we output the real Data Studio report, not a picture of one. How it solves the problem: the interview plus the commentable prototype replace hours of clicking and design trial and error. USP: the harness (procedural, semantic and episodic memory) plus a compiled recipe that a Playwright engine replays, so the expensive model is only used for decisions, not clicks.

body: Four parts with written contracts: the web app (frontend), the harness and API (backend), the dsengine CLI (engine) and the release checks.
The harness runs an ADK 2.0 graph with Gemini planner and worker models; three memories (episodic retrieval: planned).
Data lives in BigQuery: one SQL view per build.
The engine replays a compiled recipe in Data Studio with Playwright.
The next six slides open each layer.
slides.notes: This is the map for the next six slides: parts and data flow, the harness memories, the ADK graph, the token economy, the recipe and engine, and the Cloud Run deployment.

added.title: Parts and data flow
added.notes: The four parts and how data moves: the web app calls the harness API; the harness loads data into BigQuery, calls Gemini and hands a compiled recipe to dsengine, which builds the report in Data Studio. Each arrow is a written contract.

added.title: The harness: three memories
added.notes: Procedural memory is skill files, semantic memory is an OKF bundle (no vector store), episodic memory is SQLite with FTS5. After every five finished builds a cheaper model will consolidate episodes into facts (planned). Every run is traced for the eval loop.

added.title: ADK graph and repair loop
added.notes: The ADK 2.0 Workflow graph: a router sends each request to its node. LLM nodes are yellow, code nodes gray. Validate checks the spec and sends errors back to the LLM node, the repair loop, before anything is rendered or built.

added.title: Token economy
added.notes: How we keep the model cheap: the spec is the single truth, comments become small JSON patches, the recipe is compiled by code not generated, each node gets only the context it needs, and the cheaper worker model takes the routine calls.

added.title: Recipe and engine
added.notes: The Dashboard Spec compiles into recipe.jsonl, one operation per line. dsengine replays it with Playwright on the signed-in Chrome and streams one event per operation, so the build view shows progress live. Only the closed catalog of 12 component types is allowed.

added.title: Cloud Run deployment
added.notes: Planned deployment: one Cloud Run service behind a shared access code, state on a GCS volume, secrets in Secret Manager. The Data Studio build runs through dss-agent on the user's machine, because the Google session stays in the user's own signed-in Chrome.

body: Google: Gemini API (planner and worker models), BigQuery, Data Studio, Cloud Run, Cloud Storage, Secret Manager, Cloud Build.
Agent: Google ADK 2.0 Workflow graph; skills as Markdown files; OKF knowledge bundle; SQLite with FTS5.
Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, REST plus server-sent events, uv.
Engine: Playwright driving a signed-in Chrome.
Frontend: TypeScript web app built with Vite on Node 20.
slides.notes: Everything Google-native where it matters: Gemini for reasoning, BigQuery for data, Data Studio as the output, Cloud Run for hosting. ADK 2.0 is the only orchestrator; there is no vector store, the OKF bundle replaces RAG.
